passage: Aadhya here, writing down what I saw of my flatmate Vivek's app project this week. Until dinner on Tuesday, Vivek kept rearranging the booking screens: six tabs, then a side menu, then tabs again, muttering that every layout hid something important. Around nine he closed the laptop and said, "I'm done, I can't see it." He watched a cricket highlights video and went to bed. At breakfast he was already sketching on a napkin. "One screen," he said. "The list on top and the button fixed at the bottom. I was trying to make it hold everything. It didn't need to." I can't know what went on in his head overnight, but the fix took him ten minutes. He says sleep did the sorting.

Tuesday evening. Anirban had been staring at the layout for the library kiosk app since four. Two screens for search, three for borrowing, and none of them fit together. At nine his friend Ayesha knocked. "Dinner. You've been muttering at that screen for five hours."
He shut the laptop without saving a new version. "It's not coming. I'll leave it."
Wednesday morning. He woke early and, while brushing his teeth, saw it: why were search and borrowing separate at all? One screen, with a borrow button beside each result. He sketched it on the back of an envelope before breakfast.
Thursday. He showed Ayesha the new layout on his phone. Five screens had become two.
"You fixed it overnight?" she asked.
"I didn't fix it. I just stopped hammering at it. Sleep sorted it out."

qa.q: How many screens were there in the new layout?
How was Anirban feeling when he shut the laptop on Tuesday?
qa.a: He was tired and frustrated, since after five hours the layout still wasn't coming together.

qa.q: What else could Anirban do the next time he is stuck for hours?
qa.a: He could take a short walk or a break earlier, instead of waiting until he has spent five hours on it.

qa.q: How does Ayesha see Anirban's overnight solution?
qa.a: Ayesha is surprised and curious, asking if he fixed it overnight after seeing him mutter at the screen for hours.

Abhinav, you've been stuck on that engine design all evening. Let your Sumit Mama tell you a story from when I was in my third year.
I had to design a water pump mount for my project. For two days I drew version after version. Nothing balanced. One night I stayed till midnight in the drawing hall, getting angrier with every eraser mark.
My professor came in to lock up and said, "Go home. Sleep. Come back tomorrow." I thought he was being lazy.
But I went. And the next morning, walking to the college bus, I saw a water tank on a roof, held up on three legs, not four. Three legs, beta! The mount could sit on three points and never rock.
I drew it in ten minutes. Two days of struggle, and one night's sleep gave me what I needed.
So close the laptop. Eat. Sleep. See it tomorrow.

qa.q: What did Sumit see on the roof the next morning?
qa.a: He saw a water tank on a roof, held up on three legs, not four.

qa.q: How was Sumit feeling at midnight in the drawing hall?
qa.a: He was frustrated and angry, getting angrier with every eraser mark after two days of failing.

qa.q: When the professor told Sumit to go home, what could Sumit have chosen instead, and what might have happened?
qa.a: He could have stayed and kept drawing, but he would likely have stayed stuck and angry and never noticed the three-legged idea.

qa.q: How might the professor have seen Sumit that night?
qa.a: The professor probably saw a tired student going in circles and knew rest would help more than more hours at the desk.
